record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the eighth international conference on fuzzy set theory and applications
record.original_question: A 3-copula C has three marginal 2-copulas C12(x, y) = C(x, y, 1), C23(y, z) = C(1, y, z), and C13(x, z) = C(x, 1, z). A triple (C12, C23, C13) obtained this way is called compatible. Given a triple (C, D, E) of 2-copulas, characterize exactly when it is compatible. Also, for a fixed 2-copula E, determine all pairs (C, D) for which (C, D, E) is compatible, and for fixed 2-copulas C and D, determine all 2-copulas E for which (C, D, E) is compatible.

evidence.quote: A (two-dimensional) copula is a function C : [0, 1]^2 -> [0, 1] such that C(0, x) = C(x, 0) = 0 and C(1, x) = C(x, 1) = x for all x in [0, 1].
Each 3-copula C induces three marginal 2-copulas C12, C23, and C13 given by C12(x, y) = C(x, y, 1), C23(y, z) = C(1, y, z), and C13(x, z) = C(x, 1, z).
For a given triplet of 2-copulas (C, D, E), find a characterization ensuring its compatibility.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A two-dimensional copula (2-copula) is a function C:[0,1]^2 → [0,1] satisfying C(0,x)=C(x,0)=0 and C(1,x)=C(x,1)=x for all x in [0,1], together with the standard 2-increasing property: for all 0 ≤ x1 ≤ x2 ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ y1 ≤ y2 ≤ 1, C(x2,y2) - C(x2,y1) - C(x1,y2) + C(x1,y1) ≥ 0. A three-dimensional copula (3-copula) is a function C:[0,1]^3 → [0,1] that is grounded, has uniform univariate margins (C(1,1,x)=C(1,x,1)=C(x,1,1)=x), and is 3-increasing.

Every 3-copula C induces three bivariate marginal 2-copulas:
  C12(x,y) = C(x,y,1),  C23(y,z) = C(1,y,z),  C13(x,z) = C(x,1,z).
An ordered triple (C12, C23, C13) of 2-copulas is called compatible if there exists at least one 3-copula C whose three bivariate margins are precisely C12, C23, and C13.

Solve the following three problems.

(a) Give an exact characterization, in terms of intrinsic properties of (C, D, E), of when an arbitrary triple (C, D, E) of 2-copulas is compatible.

(b) For an arbitrary but fixed 2-copula E, determine the set of all pairs (C, D) of 2-copulas such that (C, D, E) is compatible.

(c) For arbitrary but fixed 2-copulas C and D, determine the set of all 2-copulas E such that (C, D, E) is compatible.
artifact.status_search_result: The compatibility problem for three 2-copulas as margins of a 3-copula is a long-standing open problem in copula theory. Partial results and sufficient conditions exist (e.g., work on Fréchet classes by Dall'Aglio, Durante–Sempi, Quesada-Molina et al., and recent work on "directly compatible copulas" in 2025), but no complete characterization of compatible triples is known. Hence the problem remains open with only partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Copulas: compatibility and Fréchet classes
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the compatibility problem of bivariate copulas as marginals of a multivariate copula and the associated Fréchet classes.
status_evidence.claim: The compatibility problem for bivariate copulas is an active research topic with only partial characterizations available.

status_evidence.title: Some advances in the study of the compatibility of three bivariate copulas
status_evidence.snippet: Provides advances and sufficient conditions on when three bivariate copulas are compatible.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial advances (sufficient conditions, special constructions) are known; a full characterization is not given.

status_evidence.title: Directly compatible copulas
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work introducing the notion of directly compatible copulas, indicating that compatibility characterization is still being investigated.
status_evidence.claim: Research as of 2025 continues to study compatibility, indicating the general problem remains open.
